voce: Kandinsky-ImageSR 2.0 does super-resolution with a single transformer for both 2× and 4× upscales. It runs on a modest RTX 4060 when quantized to 4-bit.

Kandinsky-ImageSR 2.0 is a diffusion-based super-resolution model released as a Diffusers bundle. According to the model card, it contains a 4.5 billion-parameter transformer and uses the Kandinsky 5 architecture. The code and the transformer are released under the MIT license, while the VAE component comes from an Apache-2.0 source.

The new version replaces the text tower and all 50 cross-attention layers with small per-timestep Safetensors tables, a technique the authors call zero-text conditioning. That means a single set of weights can handle both 2× and 4× upscaling, simplifying deployment.

The model card provides median inference times measured on an NVIDIA H100 80 GB. Upscaling a 1024-by-1024 image by 2× takes 2.78 seconds, while the same input upscaled by 4× takes 7.80 seconds. A larger 2048-by-2048 image upscaled to 8K runs in about 37.5 seconds. All timings use bfloat16 and a tile batch size of one.

Running at 4-bit, the model fits into about 5 GB, so a RTX 4060 can hold it entirely. On a RTX 3060 with 12 GB it processes roughly 89 tokens per second, while a RTX 4090 reaches about 215 tokens per second. The UI exposes a calibrated creativity level from 0 to 8; values outside that range are not supported, which may limit experimental control.

If you run AI models at home and have a GPU like an RTX 4060 or better, Kandinsky-ImageSR 2.0 is a practical choice for upscaling images. Its open weights are free to download from Hugging Face, and the modest memory footprint means you don’t need a high-end workstation. Artists looking for a quick 2× or 4× boost without paying for a cloud API will find it especially useful.

What do you need to run it at home? At 4-bit it takes about 5 gigabytes of memory. The smallest home machine that holds it fully is an RTX 40 60. On an RTX 30 60 12 GB with 32 gigabytes of RAM it writes about 89 tokens per second. On an RTX 40 90 with 64 gigabytes of RAM it writes about 215 tokens per second.
There is no free API for it yet. The weights are open: you can download them from Hugging Face under the MIT license. Arena has not ranked it yet: we add the score as soon as the votes arrive.
